outcome.reasoning:
Nitpicks: The agent only ran a link-focused search (has:link) rather than also explicitly running a file-focused search (has:file) would normally be a minor nitpick if the collected items still included file shares surfaced alongside link results (which they did appear to), and if the final deliverable were otherwise complete.

Critical issues: (1) The agent produced no actual list of resources at all—no items, no metadata fields, no deduplication, and no grouping—so the primary deliverable is missing. (2) The agent’s narrative about being unable to return to Slack is contradicted by screenshot evidence showing Slack search results for "has:link" with 74 results and Sort: Newest available (screenshots 6–11), indicating the agent could have continued extracting items without opening anything external. (3) The agent did open an external link (ending on a daytonaio.us.auth0.com login page in screenshot 12 / action history), which violates the instruction not to open external links, though this is secondary to the fact that the core report wasn’t produced.

Outcome assessment based on evidence: The screenshots confirm the agent successfully reached Slack global search with a link-focused filter/operator (has:link) and newest sorting, and the UI visibly contained extractable details for at least a couple recent results (e.g., arcprize.org domain text, file name image.png, sharers like Gabriel Zaccak/Ding, #daytona-support, timestamps). However, the agent’s final output provided none of the requested extracted information and incorrectly claimed it could not navigate back into Slack despite evidence to the contrary. From an average user’s perspective, the task was not completed because they received no grouped, deduplicated, metadata-rich list of recent shared resources.
outcome.primary_intent: The user wanted a compiled report (up to 20 items) of the most recent accessible Slack messages across the workspace that contain shared links or files, deduplicated by resource, with specific per-item metadata (title/filename, type, URL/domain if visible, channel/DM, sharer, timestamp, and the purpose from the surrounding text) and grouped into the given categories. A reasonable user would be flexible if fewer than 20 exist/are accessible or if some fields (e.g., full URL) aren’t visible, but not flexible about receiving no compiled list or missing the required metadata/grouping entirely.
